title: Timers and Scheduling APIs knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Timers and Scheduling APIs?
options: Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Keep synchronous callbacks short, measure delay, and avoid assuming a precise ordering where the API does not guarantee it.
questions.answer_key: Keep synchronous callbacks short, measure delay, and avoid assuming a precise ordering where the API does not guarantee it.
questions.explanation: Keep synchronous callbacks short, measure delay, and avoid assuming a precise ordering where the API does not guarantee it. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Timers and Scheduling APIs implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.

questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
